title: Circular Letter DCP 26-08-125: the Department's current requirements for pharmacist prescribing of hormonal contraceptive patches and oral hormonal contraceptives
subtopic: Department guidance on pharmacist contraceptive prescribing: supply, age, refills, training, NPI and registration
rule_summary: Circular Letter DCP 26-08-125, dated August 25, 2026, from the Director of the Bureau of Health Professions Licensure to Massachusetts licensed pharmacists, primary care practitioners and reproductive health care practitioners, rescinds and replaces DCP 25-04-124. It states that M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19F, as implemented by 105 CMR 700.000, authorizes licensed pharmacists practicing in Massachusetts to prescribe and dispense hormonal contraceptive patches, oral hormonal contraceptives, medications used for prevention of HIV, and medications used for prevention and treatment of sexually transmitted infections; that although there is no requirement to prescribe these medications, the letter provides guidance to pharmacists who choose to do so; and that a pharmacist is not required to obtain a Massachusetts Controlled Substance Registration (MCSR) as long as the prescribing and dispensing both occur at a single pharmacy location. Its General Prescribing Requirements are: (a) only FDA-approved medications authorized by M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19F and contained within the letter may be prescribed by a pharmacist; (b) the pharmacist must obtain a National Provider Identifier (NPI); (c) patient counseling and education are conducted on the proper use, risks and side effects of the selected product; (d) the medication is prescribed only in accordance with the manufacturer's approved labeling or statewide guidance; (e) the patient is provided a written record of the product that has been prescribed and dispensed; (f) the product is dispensed as soon as practicable after the pharmacist issues the prescription; (g) all activities related to the prescribing and dispensing are documented and readily available; (h) the patient is referred to, or advised to consult with, a clinical provider, or if the patient provides consent, the pharmacist notifies the patient's primary care practitioner upon the prescribing and dispensing of the selected product; (i) the pharmacist must maintain continued competency regarding current guidelines, continuing education programs being one way to maintain competency; and (j) pharmacists are encouraged to enroll in MassHealth for the limited purpose of ordering and referring services covered by MassHealth, to allow MassHealth reimbursement for pharmacists' prescriptions to MassHealth enrollees. Under its heading Hormonal Contraceptive Patches and Oral Hormonal Contraceptives the letter states that a pharmacist may prescribe hormonal contraceptive patches and oral hormonal contraceptives, regardless of whether the product is over-the-counter or prescription-only, to patients of any age, provided that: prior to prescribing, the patient completes a pharmacy-provided self-screening risk assessment tool based on the current United States Medical Eligibility Criteria for Contraceptive Use; a valid prescription for up to, but not more than, a 12-month supply is generated; lack of a clinical visit with a primary care practitioner or reproductive health care practitioner does not preclude a pharmacist from issuing a prescription with refills; a scheduled appointment with the pharmacist shall not be required for the purpose of the prescribing or dispensing of a hormonal contraceptive patch or oral hormonal contraceptive; and, prior to prescribing, the pharmacist completes a training program that addresses the objectives the letter lists. Training programs accredited by the American Council on Pharmaceutical Education (ACPE) or Interprofessional Continuing Education (IPCE) are recommended, documentation of completed training must be provided upon request, and the program objectives must include describing the mechanism of action and differentiating between types of hormonal contraceptive products, assessing patient eligibility for hormonal contraceptive use and recommended products, educating patients on proper use, risks and benefits of various contraceptive products, educating patients on strategies to reduce risk of sexually transmitted infections, and documenting patient care visits related to hormonal contraceptive products.
exam_relevance: Tests the conditions the Department's current guidance attaches to pharmacist contraceptive prescribing that neither the statute nor the regulation states, including the 12-month supply ceiling, the absence of an age limit, refills without a clinical visit, the NPI, the training objectives and the single-location condition on the registration statement.

exceptions: A pharmacist is not required to obtain a Massachusetts Controlled Substance Registration as long as the prescribing and dispensing both occur at a single pharmacy location.
Lack of a clinical visit with a primary care practitioner or reproductive health care practitioner does not preclude a pharmacist from issuing a prescription with refills.
common_confusions: Treating accreditation of the training program by ACPE or IPCE as a requirement; the letter recommends accredited programs, requires that the program address the listed objectives, and requires documentation of completed training to be provided upon request.
Assuming a minimum patient age; the letter states that a pharmacist may prescribe to patients of any age.
Assuming an over-the-counter product falls outside pharmacist prescribing; the letter applies regardless of whether the product is over-the-counter or prescription-only.
Reading the registration statement as unconditional; the letter conditions it on the prescribing and dispensing both occurring at a single pharmacy location.
Treating the letter as requiring pharmacists to prescribe; it states that there is no requirement to prescribe these medications.
verification_notes: Read the full text of Circular Letter DCP 26-08-125 (three-page PDF published on mass.gov as Pharmacist Prescribing of Certain Medications, last updated 2026-08-25) on 2026-09-16, reached from the Policies and Circular Letters list on the Board of Registration in Pharmacy's Pharmacy Practice Resources page and from the Drug Control Program's news page for DCP 26-08-125. The letter's sections on HIV prevention and on sexually transmitted infection prevention and treatment are not stated in this record.
